sections.heading: The River Sons
sections.summary: Tethys and Ocean have many sons, the river gods.

cards.label: Tethys
cards.general: A Titan goddess and the mother of rivers and water goddesses.
cards.here: She bears Ocean these river sons.

cards.label: Ocean
cards.general: Ocean, or Oceanus, is the god of the great river believed to circle the world.
cards.here: He is the father of the Rivers.

cards.label: Rivers
cards.general: For the Greeks, a river could also be a god.
cards.here: The named rivers are children of Tethys and Ocean.

cards.label: Nile
cards.general: The great river of Egypt.

cards.label: Alpheus
cards.general: A river in southern Greece, flowing past Olympia.

cards.label: Eridanus
cards.general: A mythical river whose location was understood differently by different ancient writers.

cards.label: Strymon
cards.general: A river flowing into the northern Aegean Sea.

cards.label: Maeander
cards.general: A famously winding river in what is now western Turkey.

cards.label: Ister

cards.label: Phasis
cards.general: A river at the eastern end of the Black Sea, in what is now Georgia.

cards.label: Rhesus
cards.general: A river name associated with the region around Troy.

cards.label: Achelous
cards.general: A major river in western Greece and its god.
cards.here: His swirling waters gleam like silver.

cards.label: Nessus

cards.label: Rhodius
cards.general: A river in the region around Troy.

cards.label: Haliacmon

cards.label: Heptaporus

cards.label: Grenicus

cards.label: Aesepus

cards.label: Simois

cards.label: Peneus

cards.label: Scamander

sections.heading: Ocean’s Many Daughters
sections.translation:
Tethys also bore a sacred family of daughters.
Across the earth, they nurture the young,
together with Lord Apollo and the Rivers:
this is the task Zeus has given them.

They are Peitho, Admete, Ianthe, Electra,
Doris, Prymno, and godlike Urania;
Hippo, Clymene, Rhodea, Callirhoe,
Zeuxo, Clytie, Idyia, Pasithoe,
Plexaura, Galaxaura, and lovely Dione;
Melobosis, Thoe, and beautiful Polydora;
Cerceis, lovely in form, and wide-eyed Pluto;
Perseis, Ianeira, Acaste, Xanthe,
lovely Petraea, Menestho, Europa,
Metis, Eurynome, and Telesto in her saffron-colored robe;
Chryseis, Asia, and enchanting Calypso;
Eudora, Tyche, Amphiro, Ocyroe,
and Styx, the foremost of them all.

These are the eldest daughters born to Ocean and Tethys,
but there are many others.
There are three thousand slender-ankled daughters of Ocean,
scattered far and wide, watching over the earth
and the depths of the waters everywhere alike—
glorious children of goddesses.

And there are just as many other Rivers,
sons of Ocean whom the noble Tethys bore,
whose waters rush and roar.
It would be hard for a mortal to tell all their names,
but people living beside each river know its name.
sections.summary: Ocean and Tethys have three thousand daughters who care for the young and watch over land and water. They also have just as many river sons.

cards.label: Daughters of Ocean
cards.general: These water goddesses are often called Oceanids.
cards.here: Hesiod names the eldest, then says there are three thousand altogether.

cards.label: Apollo
cards.general: A god associated with music, prophecy, healing, and the protection of the young.
cards.here: He helps the Rivers and Ocean’s daughters nurture the young.

cards.label: Zeus
cards.general: The king of the gods.
cards.here: He assigns the daughters their task.

cards.label: Peitho
cards.general: Her name means persuasion; she is also associated with its divine power.

sections.heading: Sun, Moon, and Dawn
sections.translation:
Theia, yielding to Hyperion in love,
bore great Helios, the Sun, and bright Selene, the Moon,
and Eos, the Dawn, who shines for everyone on earth
and for the immortal gods who live in the wide sky.
sections.summary: Theia and Hyperion have three children: Sun, Moon, and Dawn.

cards.label: Theia
cards.general: One of the Titans, an older generation of gods.
cards.here: The mother of Helios, Selene, and Eos.

cards.label: Hyperion
cards.general: One of the Titans.
cards.here: The father of Helios, Selene, and Eos.

cards.label: Helios
cards.general: The Sun as a god.

cards.label: Selene
cards.general: The Moon as a goddess.

cards.label: Eos
cards.general: The goddess of dawn, the first light of morning.
cards.here: She brings light to people and gods.

cards.label: Immortal
cards.general: Living forever; unable to die.

sections.heading: Winds and Starry Skies
sections.translation:
Eurybia, shining among goddesses,
joined Crius in love and bore him
great Astraeus, Pallas, and Perses,
whose knowledge set him apart from everyone.

Eos lay with Astraeus, goddess with god,
and bore him the fierce-hearted Winds:
Zephyrus, who clears the sky, swift-moving Boreas,
and Notus.

After the Winds, Eos, born at daybreak,
bore Eosphorus, the Morning Star,
and the gleaming stars that crown the sky.
sections.summary: Eurybia and Crius have three sons. Eos and one of those sons, Astraeus, become the parents of the Winds and stars.

cards.label: Eurybia
cards.general: A goddess, daughter of Earth and the Sea.
cards.here: With Crius, she has Astraeus, Pallas, and Perses.

cards.label: Crius
cards.general: One of the Titans, an older generation of gods.
cards.here: The father of Astraeus, Pallas, and Perses.

cards.label: Astraeus
cards.general: A god associated with stars.
cards.here: With Eos, he fathers the Winds and stars.

cards.label: Pallas
cards.general: A god who shares his name with other mythical figures.
cards.here: A son of Eurybia and Crius.

cards.label: Perses
cards.general: A son of Eurybia and Crius.
cards.here: Hesiod singles him out for his knowledge.

cards.label: Eos
cards.general: The goddess of dawn.
cards.here: She is the mother of the Winds and stars; “born at daybreak” is a poetic title for her.

cards.label: Winds
cards.general: The Greeks imagined winds as gods with their own names and characters.
cards.here: Three are named as children of Eos and Astraeus.

cards.label: Zephyrus
cards.general: The god of the west wind.
cards.here: He is described as clearing the sky.

cards.label: Boreas
cards.general: The god of the north wind.

cards.label: Notus
cards.general: The god of the south wind.

cards.label: Eosphorus
cards.general: The Morning Star: the planet Venus when it appears before sunrise.
cards.here: A divine child of Eos and Astraeus.

uncertainties: In line 365, λίμνης can describe a lake or a broader body of water, including the sea. “The depths of the waters” leaves that range open.
In line 379, Zephyrus’s epithet ἀργέστην can suggest brightness or the clearing of the sky. The translation follows the sky-clearing sense.
